source.title: Evaluating natural language processing models with generalization metrics that do not need access to any training or testing data
source.authors: Yaoqing Yang; Ryan Theisen; Liam Hodgkinson; Joseph Gonzalez; K. Ramchandran; Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: Extends a generalization-gap metric comparison to NLP Transformers; it measures PAC-Bayesian metrics, including magnitude-aware flatness, against the training-test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports correlations of generalization metrics with BLEU and the generalization gap. Figure-only metric values are not reconstructed. The broader comparisons among metric families do not establish the specific V7 claim about magnitude-scaled perturbations ranking gaps better than norm- and margin-based measures.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance against training–test BLEU gaps in Transformers, extending V7's correlational question to NLP. It also compares this metric with norm- and margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that popular metrics correlate well with NLP generalization gaps, while heavy-tail spectral metrics are more useful for predicting model quality without data access. They recommend further investigation, including weaknesses on suboptimally trained models.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares generalization metrics on machine translation Transformers and NLP pretrained models, rather than the stated CNN-family perturbation analysis on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlations vary across metric families and hyperparameter settings; the text reports Simpson's paradox with particularly large learning rates and reversed trends for some metrics across model series.

fits_no_version.finding: Heavy-tail spectral metrics predict held-out NLP performance, with sensitivity to training quality and the hyperparameter varied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-spectrum shape metrics can predict NLP model quality without accessing training or testing data.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 compares Transformer training with dropout 0.1 and without dropout, describing underfitting and overfitting respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout changes fitting dynamics in machine-translation Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: Accurately ranking generalization gaps need not accurately rank held-out performance when training performance differs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization-gap ranking is insufficient for model selection when training errors vary.

record.problems: The V7-relevant metric result is figure-only and is not isolated in the text. The study's NLP setting and correlation target do not establish the version's specific ranking claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The available gap correlations for other metrics are figure-only aggregate comparisons and do not isolate results bearing on V7.

Widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects in fully connected and convolutional classifiers, including small-data and excessive-dropout regimes.

The original CNN setting, similarly low training losses, and training–test classification-error gaps. Exact magnitude-aware correlations and their uncertainty cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
Retraining after removing memorized versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Separate magnitude-aware flatness results by varied hyperparameter. The displayed metric ordering puts pacbayes_mag_flatness first when learning rate varies but near the bottom when width varies. Recover actual correlations before assigning directional support or challenge labels.
Kendall's tau corroboration of the time-wise magnitude-aware flatness versus gap analysis; the text reports results similar to Figure 4, but numerical metric-specific values are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V7. Figure ordering supports comparative-ranking qualifications, but the supplied text does not establish metric-specific correlation magnitudes or signs. Poor prediction of test BLEU alone does not challenge V7, which concerns the generalization gap.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.

The study evaluates a magnitude-aware PAC-Bayesian flatness metric against the generalization gap on NLP Transformers, but the displayed result is figure-only and does not isolate that metric's result or establish the version's comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Transformers trained on WMT14
rows.size_stated: 360 trained models across settings; individual model sizes not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured the rank correlation of PAC-Bayesian generalization metrics with the generalization gap across training settings.
rows.measure: Spearman rank correlation with generalization gap
rows.note: The figure shows distributions across 360 settings; the supplied text does not state a separable result for pacbayes_mag_flatness.
rows.check: The analysis is time-wise: correlations are computed over epochs separately within each of 360 training settings, then summarized, rather than computed across 360 final models. Isolate pacbayes_mag_flatness instead of grouping all PAC-Bayesian metrics. The supplied figure text does not preserve its correlation values or distribution. The gap is training BLEU minus test BLEU; perturbation tolerance uses increased training loss.

source_check.correct: Figure 4 summarizes correlations calculated over training epochs separately within each of 360 hyperparameter settings, rather than correlations across the 360 models. The generalization gap is training BLEU minus test BLEU. No numerical correlation specific to pacbayes_mag_flatness is stated.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.1–3.2.2, pages 7–10; Figure 4b and its caption.
source_check.problem: The operation's across-training-settings wording omits the within-model, over-epoch correlation axis; the pack's verdict fix correctly identifies this.

relationships.condition: Relative ranking of gap predictors in WMT14 Transformers across training epochs and when network width varies
relationships.reason: The metric ordering in Figures 4b and 10b places pacbayes_mag_flatness below several norm- and margin-based measures, limiting extension of V7's comparative superiority to these settings. This uses figure-label ordering in the supplied text, not reconstructed correlation values; R1 lacks these comparisons.
relationships.display_finding: The available evidence does not confirm that sharpness performed worse than norm and margin measures, as reported. Correlations with BLEU gaps were calculated across epochs within each training setting.
